        ### Question
        A 35-year-old woman undergoes a Pap smear after 5 years without prior control and the diagnosis is SIL (high-grade intraepithelial lesion). The correct behavior to follow is:

        ### Options
        opa. Make colposcopy. If it is normal, schedule a conization.
opb. Confirm the cytology with a biopsy of the cervix under colposcopic control.
opc. Repeat cytology to confirm diagnosis.
opd. Make HPV virus typing. Perform conization if the HPV test is positive for high-risk virus.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "High-grade SIL diagnosis" -> "Need for further evaluation" -> "Colposcopy recommended" -> "Colposcopy performed" -> "Normal colposcopy" -> "Conization scheduled" -> 70%
CHAIN: "High-grade SIL diagnosis" -> "Need for confirmation" -> "Cervical biopsy under colposcopy" -> "Biopsy confirms diagnosis" -> "Appropriate treatment planned" -> 85%
CHAIN: "High-grade SIL diagnosis" -> "Need for confirmation" -> "Repeat cytology" -> "Cytology may not confirm diagnosis" -> "Potential delay in treatment" -> 50%
CHAIN: "High-grade SIL diagnosis" -> "Need for HPV status" -> "HPV typing performed" -> "High-risk HPV positive" -> "Conization considered" -> 60%
